title: Understanding Grease Blockages in Kitchen Drain Pipes
description: A practical lesson on how liquid cooking fats solidify inside cold drain pipes, narrowing the flow diameter and causing deep sink clogs.
image_prompt: A photorealistic vertical 9:16 close-up photograph of a kitchen sink plumbing setup inside an under-sink cabinet. A clean, white PVC drain pipe extending from a standard P-trap is shown with a clear side cutaway view. Inside the cutaway pipe section, a thick, realistic layer of solidified yellowish grease and fine food debris coats the interior walls of the pipe, severely restricting the internal flow diameter. The surrounding plumbing includes a stainless steel sink basin underside, realistic threaded slip-nuts, and clean PVC solvent-weld fittings. Bright, realistic task lighting highlights the contrast between the clean pipe exterior and the greasy buildup inside. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no arrows, no labels.
visual_story: A detailed cutaway view under a kitchen sink demonstrating how liquid fat coats the internal wall of a PVC waste line, restricting water flow.

on_image_text.explanation: Liquid fats rapidly cool inside cold drain pipes, clinging to pipe walls and catching passing food scraps.
on_image_text.takeaway: Scrape pans into the trash and wipe with paper towels before washing.
